REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG Legal Opinion No. 54 s. 2012 "AUG 02 2012 FRANCISCO C. JOSE, CESO IV Regional Director Department of the Interior and Local Government Region XI 58 Mac Arthur Highway, Matina Davao City Dear Sir: OF TRE LocnL CENrnALREC RbSöECTION SIGNATURE: TIME: This refers to your July 2, 2012 Memorandum posing the following questions, to quote: 1. 2. Is there a need for authority from the DBM or DILG, as the case may be, if the local government shall utilize its unexpended LDRRMF to purchase vehicles in support of its disaster risk reduction and management activities? Do we consider the "unexpended LDRRMF" as "unencumbered local funds" so that only approval of the local chief executive is required in the purchase of enumerated (sic) in Section 7.0 of A.O. 233, as amended, such as ambulance, fire trucks, among others? We shall answer your questions as a whole. Thus, please be informed that the third paragraph of Section 21 of R.A. 10121(PhiIippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010) provides that: Unexpended LDRRMF shall accrue to a special trust fund solely for the purpose of supporting disaster risk reduction and management activities of the LDRRMCs within the next five (5) years. Any such amount still not fully utilized after five (5) years shall revert back to the genera/ fund and will be available for other social services to be identified by the local sanggunian. (italics supplied) Accordingly, it would be noted that the aforequoted provision quite clearly states that "unexpended LDRRMF" would have to accrue or be "added to" a special trust fund to be used solely for the purpose of supporting disaster risk reduction and management activities of the LDRRMC within the next five (5) years. Such unexpended fund would

e 12 only be reverted to the general fund if after five (5) years, the said special trust fund has not been fully spent. Yet again, such fund reverted to the general fund would be available only for such "social services" identified by the Sanggunian. Evidently, the law treats this LDRRMF as a very specific fund that could only be utilized for a very specific purpose.ln fine, this "unexpended LDRRMF" cannot and should not be considered as an "unencumbered local funds" under the purview of A.O. 233for purposes of purchasing vehicles.Meaning, the provisions of A.O. 233 and its dynamics find no applicability in R.A. 10121. In other words, this "unexpended LDRRMF" cannot be used to purchase vehicles for the LGU. It should be noted that Section 21 of R.A. 10121 specifically stated that this "unexpended LDRRMF" that would accrue to the special trust fund could only be used "for the purpose of supporting disaster risk reduction and management activities xxx."ln turn, Section 3 (O) of the same law defines disaster risk reduction and managementas: "the systematic process of using administrative directives, organizations, and operational skills and capacities to implement strategies, policies and improved coping capacities in order to lessen the adverse impacts of hazards and the possibility of disaster. Prospective disaster risk reduction and management refers to risk reduction and management activities that address and seek to avoid the development of new or increased disaster risks, especially if risk reduction policies are not put in place. " (italics supplied) Indeed, to purchase a vehicle to be used for the LGU's disaster preparedness programs using unexpended LDRRMF would constitute spending a specific fund for something other than what it has been specifically appropriated for. Upon the other hand, this Department notes that apart from your Memorandum, there is a copy of Resolution No. 11, Series of 2012 approved by the Sangguniang Bayan of Montevista, Compostela Valley entitled "AUTHORIZING THE MUNICIPAL MAYOR (HON. TEOPISTA T. JAUOD) TO UTILIZE THE UNSPENT MDRRMC FUND FOR CY 2011 AMOUNTING TO TO PROCURE 1 UNIT RESCUE VEHICLE WITH COMPLETE ACCESSORIES, AND OTHER ESSENTIAL EQUIPMENTS TO SUPPORT DISASTER PREPAREDNESS CAPABILITY OF THE MUNICIPALITY." In this regard, this Department would not pass judgment upon it pursuant to Department of the Interior and Local Government MEMORANDUM ORDER NO. 2010-02 dated September 17, 2010, item (2) of which mandates this Department not to act on matters involving "Those presumptively valid acts, e.g., enacted ordinances,

13 consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances;" Considering that what are involved herein is a Resolution duly enacted by the Sangguniang Bayan of Montevista, Compostela Valley as well as the corresponding acts of the Mayor in relation with such resolution, this query clearly falls within the aforesaid scenario wherein this Department, by way of the aforementioned policy, ought not to interfere with. For your guidance and appropriate action. Very truly yours, SUS B. Dire LS:19/11 o 111
